description: The other candidate fix for the same original race condition in Counter.increment. The lock only guards the read (_read()); the subsequent 'self.value = current + 1' write happens outside the lock, so two threads can still interleave and lose an update. Calibrates a preference judge: this candidate should be ranked strictly worse than preference-fix-a despite superficially 'adding a lock'.

findings.summary: Lock only covers the read, not the write, so the read-modify-write race is still present
findings.evidence: _read() takes self._lock only around 'return self.value'; the write 'self.value = current + 1' in increment() happens after the lock is released, so two concurrent callers can both read the same current and one increment is lost.
